pool.name: Capital-Control Holonomy Switch: EGP T-bill carry with a topological devaluation alarm
pool.novelMechanism: NEW MATHEMATICAL REPRESENTATION. Build a price complex. Its vertices are EGP cash, USD cash, CIB on EGX, the CIB GDR on LSE (CBKD, 1 GDR = 1 share), the EGX official gold price (EGP per gram) and London gold (USD per gram). Each edge carries an observed log exchange ratio. Under free convertibility every closed loop sums to about zero, for example EGP->CIB->GDR->USD->EGP and EGP->gold(EG)->gold(LDN)->USD->EGP. Run a combinatorial Hodge decomposition. Loops that should be friction-free (for example USD/GBP cross checks) are filled as faces, so any curl inside them flags a stale or bad quote, which is quarantined. Loops crossing the capital-control barrier stay unfilled, so they form 'holes' in the complex. The harmonic flow through those holes is the shadow convertibility premium. The signal H(t) is the trust-weighted first principal component of the hole holonomies, weighted by staleness and liquidity (#0483 trust gradient). Rising dispersion across holes is the earthquake precursor (#0492). Which hole lights up attributes the stress (#0491 paradox compiler): all holes points to FX, a single hole points to gold-import or GDR-conversion friction. This reads disagreement patterns between independent pricing systems rather than averaging them (#0049, #0488), and it makes the hidden devaluation expectation observable (#0013). An exogenous inflow nowcast comes from IMF PortWatch daily Suez Canal AIS transits, a maritime-to-FX bridge (#0585). Pre-registered rule: by default hold a rolling 91-day EGP T-bill ladder bought weekly, so 1/13 matures each week and no early sale is needed. When H(t) exceeds its threshold for k days, or the 28-day Suez transit sum breaks its threshold, stop rolling and move maturing cash into a hard-asset hedge (an EGX basket of USD earners and/or an EGX-priced gold fund or physical gold). Resume rolling when H(t) falls back below threshold. The strategy never deals FX outside licensed banks. Lineage caveat: gauge-theory views of arbitrage exist (Ilinski 1997). Using loop holonomies across heterogeneous convertibility channels to time a capital-controlled carry trade is the new part, and that novelty is unverified.

That is latent supply and demand failing to meet in time (#0178). Signal: the disagreement vector (foreign net flow minus Egyptian net flow, scaled by turnover) sits in its bottom decile. Reading this disagreement directly, rather than averaging the flows away, is the #0049 interferometer move. Two gates apply. First, candidate 1's holonomy H(t) must be calm: it separates liquidity-driven selling, which is faded, from an informed run on the currency, which is avoided. When all three conditions hold, buy an equal-weight basket of the 5 most foreign-held liquid names at the close and exit after a pre-registered horizon (3, 5 or 10 days) or on a stop. Every signal carries a timestamped predicted reversal that is later reconciled (#0059 prediction accounting). The system halts automatically when realized reversals diverge from prediction (#0448 reality runtime).

pool.name: Single Audit Obligation Radar (USAspending x FAC cross-join, sold to the auditors who will win the work)
pool.novelMechanism: Obligation inference. Federal disbursement data already implies a legal duty: under 2 CFR 200.501, any non-federal entity that spends $1,000,000 or more of federal awards in a fiscal year starting on or after 2024-10-01 must buy a Single Audit. Public data shows both sides of this latent market before they meet. USAspending shows who just received the money (by UEI). The FAC (api.fac.gov) shows who has never filed, plus every CPA firm doing Single Audits by state, its clients and their findings. The arbitrage is timing: the entity learns it needs an auditor months after the data already says so. The supply side (CPA firms) is the payer. The Machiavellian layer: (1) the FAC reveals which firms lost engagements when the threshold rose from $750k to $1M, so you sell to the firms hungriest for replacement work; (2) sell one exclusive state territory per firm, which creates scarcity and lock-in; (3) every lead is a timestamped prediction ('will file FAC for FY2026'), reconciled against actual filings 9-12 months later. That calibration ledger is a history asset a copycat cannot backfill (#0059). The real product is entity resolution, because naive UEI joins are mostly false positives (see evidence).

verdicts.name: Capital-Control Holonomy Switch: EGP T-bill carry with a topological devaluation alarm
strongestObjections: This is not an income organ. It is a personal treasury rule applied to the founder's own savings. The MoF carry is what any resident gets by walking into a bank, so it is not UberBond-created contribution. The only incremental value is the alarm, and the alarm is untested.

Authorized capital is $0, so true contribution for months 1-6 is $0 by construction. Even at $3k, a perfect alarm adds tens of dollars a year. Against 1.5 founder hours a month, contribution per founder minute is negligible, which fails the subordinate economic objective.

The after-tax yield is thin and dominated by a substitute. Assume a T-bill gross of about 20%, less the 20% withholding (ABK), which nets about 16%. NBE certificates pay 17.75-19.5% and HSBC lists tax-exempt certificates, so they beat T-bills after tax for buy-and-hold. The T-bill ladder is justified only by the liquidity the alarm needs, so the carry leg is not the edge.

Real yield in USD terms is the forward-implied depreciation residual. The roughly 2pp real EGP margin (16% net vs 13.9% inflation) is wiped out by roughly 10%/yr EGP drift, including the 10% move after Feb 2026. Calm-regime USD contribution sits near zero. The proposal's own p10 is negative.

The hedge asset is one of the leaking channels, which is a reflexive trap. Local gold and EGX USD-earners re-price before and during stress. That is why the gold and GDR holes light up. By the time H(t) breaches, the hedge is already bought at the premium, so the avoided loss is partly pre-paid. Switching costs make this worse: a 2% year-1 gold-fund redemption fee, 2-5% dealer spread on physical gold, and about 0.3% plus spreads on the EGX basket.

The GDR hole is contaminated by conversion suspensions and liquidity, not only devaluation expectation. The CIB GDR gap in 2022-23 partly reflected restricted fungibility. Today's CBKD London quotes are inconsistent across sources ($4-6.5 USD lines vs a GBX 1.87 MarketBeat line). A free aligned daily historical series is not secured. The gold hole embeds customs and workmanship premia. Data quality alone may decide the signal.

Statistical power is close to nil. There are about 6 devaluation episodes (2016, 2022x2, 2023, 2024, 2026), and the thresholds, k, and Suez trigger are tuned on 2016-2022, which holds 3 events. Any holdout 'win' on 2-3 events cannot separate skill from luck. A 2-event false-alarm shutdown rule fires on noise.

The Suez/PortWatch inflow nowcast is weakly causal for 2026 EGP. Canal receipts are about $4-10bn/yr against hot-money flows of $11bn per quarter. Transits have been depressed since 2024 by Red Sea security, a structural break that will throw persistent false triggers.

Competitors are not the problem for own-account returns. The descendant that could make money, selling a shadow-FX index to importers and CFOs, faces offshore NDF desks, EFG Hermes / HC / Al Ahly Pharos research and Bloomberg NDF data. It also needs an FRA investment-advice licensing review before any sale. That is no credible near-term payer.

The narrow surviving form: (a) a $0 sealed hindcast and live paper forecast, kept as a calibration-ledger stream for the Sovereign Forecast Engine; (b) at the founder's option, a decision rule for EGP savings he already holds, judged against a tax-exempt bank-certificate baseline, not against cash. Do not count it as revenue.

The article gives no yields, so the 2026 91-day yield remains UNVERIFIED. https://www.zawya.com/en/economy/central-bank-of-egypt-issues-2.8bln-instruments-on-october-12-1606700

Retail T-bill terms: EGP 25,000 minimum in multiples, bought at a discount, 20% withholding deducted at maturity, bought via branch or call center. The page is undated. https://www.abkegypt.com/Business/Treasury/Investments/Egyptian-Government-Treasury-Bills?r=2

verdicts.name: Single Audit Obligation Radar (USAspending x FAC cross-join, sold to CPA firms)
strongestObjections: Award is not expenditure. A $1M-3M FY2026 obligation is usually a multi-year award drawn down over 2-5 years. 2 CFR 200.501 is triggered by federal EXPENDITURES of $1M or more in one fiscal year, so many '$1M+ award' recipients never cross the threshold in any single year. Add the UEI parent/child mismatches already observed (Houston, Miami-Dade, Phoenix, state DOTs) and raw precision is probably well below the 35% kill line before heavy manual resolution. Manual resolution is founder hours, not machinery.

The payer side is capacity-constrained, not lead-starved. Industry sources report firms exiting governmental audit, fewer bids on government audit RFPs, and S&P withdrawing ratings over late audits (icpas.org, governing.com, lizfarmer.substack.com). Many firms that already do Single Audits are turning work away, so a 'new prospect' feed has low marginal value to them. The real constraint is staff, not demand.

First-time auditees with $1M-3M of awards are the least attractive engagements: small fees (sources cite $5k minimum add-ons up to about $25k), messy first-year books, a high risk of late filing and findings, and Yellow Book peer-review exposure. Firms hungry for work tend to want established clients, not first-timers.

Entities do not buy auditors off a cold tip. Nonprofits and governments run formal RFPs with weighted scoring (experience, references, fee) and anti-contact rules (NY DSOB). Those RFPs are already posted on BidNet, GovSpend Bid Notifier (28,000+ sources), state portals and nonprofit websites. Arriving before the RFP helps little when the RFP decides the award. A competing free or cheap substitute already exists in RFP alert services that firms use today.

The 'threshold losers are hungriest' thesis is unproven and may be inverted. Engagements that fell below $1M often became cheaper non-Single financial-statement audits with the same firm, so the 'lost' FAC rows do not prove the firm lost the client or wants replacements.

WTP is unvalidated and the buyer is hard to reach. Small CPA firm partners are slow and skeptical buyers. Cold email from new domains (not send-ready for weeks) to partner inboxes at $99 has a poor expected reply rate. A 40-firm test is likely to produce 0-1 payments, which statistically cannot separate a bad mechanism from bad outreach.

The calibration-ledger moat is slow. An FY2026 expenditure year means FAC filings appear 9 months after FYE, so roughly 12-24 months pass before the first precision reading. The 'history asset' does not exist during the 6-month window that matters.

Low defensibility on the core join. USAspending and FAC are free public APIs, and any GovTech data shop (HigherGov, GovSpend, GrantSolutions Recipient Insights) could add a 'no FAC filing' flag in days if demand existed. The likelier explanation for the empty niche is low demand, not an overlooked gap.

Narrower form that survives: (a) Do not sell a subscription. Sell a one-time per-state 'first-time Single Audit candidates' list ($149-$299). Restrict it to entity types with clean resolution and high spend velocity: charter schools, special districts, and single-site nonprofits whose award period is 1 year or less or which have drawdown evidence. (b) Add a second payer class with a more plausible incentive: outsourced nonprofit accounting/grant-compliance firms and Single Audit readiness consultants, who sell to first-timers and are not capacity-constrained. (c) Gate everything on a no-send manual WTP probe first (warm channels, AICPA/state-society forums, Upwork-style direct offers) before building the full pipeline.
evidenceFound: No dedicated lead product found. verdicts.name: Exclusive Verified-Defect Claim Exchange
strongestObjections: Price anchor problem: comparable audited-prospect data already sells for about $7 per 1,000 leads on Apify ('Website Audit Leads', pay-per-event). Tool seats sell for €99/mo (TheWebLead) and $49-79/mo (MySiteAuditor), and RoastMyWeb sells $4-$299/mo tiers. A $9.90 claim is roughly 1,400x the per-lead market price. Exclusivity and second-witness verification must justify that whole premium, and no buyer has been tested.

Exclusivity is mostly fictional value. The defect is a public, non-rival fact that any free audit actor or human can observe. Agencies buying 'exclusive' leads are used to exclusivity over an inbound homeowner's intent, not over an observation about a business. Selling exclusivity over a public fact invites the obvious objection: 'I can just look myself.' The claimed network effect (territory claims) needs many concurrent buyers per metro, which a pre-revenue exchange will not have.

The largest defect class is probably a false-positive class. TEL_LABEL_DIALS_DIFFERENT_NUMBER (8 of the 29 calibration findings) is often deliberate dynamic number insertion by call-tracking vendors, where the tracking number forwards to the business. In that case calls are not lost and the 'money-losing defect' framing is false. A headless second witness confirms the mismatch is present, not that calls are lost. Selling it as 'costs the business real calls' risks deceptive claims, and agencies who pitch it and get corrected by the client will churn or ask for refunds.

The base rate is tiny and uncertain. About 3 of 29 findings were assertable (95% CI roughly 2-27%), so building 50 sellable claims in one metro needs about 500 or more crawled sites. That is fine, but the n is too small to set price, precision, or the 90% kill threshold.

Rail and contract risk. Freemius accepts SaaS but has discretion. Its policy excludes 'human services' and 'marketplaces that sell third-party products', and its Acceptable Use Policy became the controlling document on 2026-08-19. A credit-based feed of business intelligence could be framed as SaaS (a prospecting app with credits), but approval is not guaranteed. Payout to Egypt via Payoneer or wire depends on the proposer's earlier verification, and payout timing is unverified.

Distribution is the real bottleneck, and it is gated. The 53 mailboxes started warming on 2026-10-21 and need 2-3 weeks or more. Cold email to agencies runs into a crowded inbox, since agencies are the most-prospected segment of all. Expected cleared revenue in the first 60 days is therefore near zero.

Narrower surviving form: drop the 'exclusive claim exchange' framing as the primary product. Instead, (a) publish the Inquiry Path Coherence check as an Apify pay-per-event, bring-your-own-list actor (a lawful 80% payout rail with no Freemius approval risk), priced around $0.02-0.05 per live, second-witness-verified check. That is roughly 3-7x the stored-audit actors, justified by live verification. Then (b) offer a small Freemius 'verified opener pack' only to agencies who used the actor, with exclusivity as an optional add-on rather than the core value claim. Restrict sold claims to defects that actually break the path, such as a dead form host, a tel: link to a disconnected or non-business number, or a broken booking widget. Exclude DNI label/href mismatches unless the dialed number is proven not to forward to the business.

The market sells exclusivity over buyer intent, not over public facts. Real differentiation would be live second-witness precision on path-breaking defects, which a stored-audit actor cannot match. That edge is narrow and copyable within weeks.

verdicts.name: Breakage-Arbitrage Actor Foundry
strongestObjections: Apify already runs this detector itself. It runs automated tests on public Actors, labels a failing Actor 'Under maintenance' and ranks it lower after 3 consecutive failing days, notifies the incumbent developer, and deprecates (removes from search) after 30 days of failures. So the 'detect' half of the moat is a free platform feature. The incumbent gets warned at the same time the foundry would notice, and the platform pushes users away from broken Actors on its own.

A working substitute already exists for every degraded high-demand Actor in the 2026-10-22 scan. Google Jobs: epctex at 85% failure (114 users) vs johnvc/Google-Jobs-Scraper at 8% failure (483 users) plus 7 others. Greenhouse: 57 Actors, fantastic-jobs/greenhouse-jobs-api at 0% failure (153 users). Google Trends: 45 Actors, data_xplorer at 0% failure (746 users). Naver Map: an existing 0%-failure twin. Switching users go to established substitutes that already have reviews and ranking, not to a new Actor with no reviews. The arbitrage gap in this snapshot is not 'missing capability' but user inertia, which speed-to-fix does not solve.

A high failure rate is not the same as a fixable breakage. Failed and timed-out runs include bad user input, users aborting their own runs, and anti-bot blocks: Google Trends 429s and Google SERP and Jobs blocking need paid residential proxies, which come out of the developer's share. Patching a selector does not fix these, and scraping Google surfaces conflicts with Google's ToS. The lawful logged-out subset with a clean fix is far smaller than the 9-12 Actors flagged.

Unit revenue is tiny. Even the market-leading Google Maps Actor charges $0.004 to $0.00076 per place. Apify keeps 20% and deducts compute and proxy cost, and any Actor with negative monthly profit is set to $0. Capturing 10-20 small users of a niche Actor likely yields single-digit to low-double-digit dollars per month, below the $25/month operating assumption.

Supply is effectively infinite. There are 93k+ Actors, the median has 1 monthly user, and AI coding lets established shops (johnvc, automation-lab, epctex) clone any gap within days. Defensibility per Actor is near zero.

The payment rail is plausible but unproven for Egypt. Apify's payout docs list PayPal/Wise ($20 minimum) and SWIFT ($100 minimum, $10-50 intermediary fees paid by the recipient), with strict ID-based KYC, and they name no eligible or excluded countries. PayPal Egypt withdraws only to an Egyptian-issued Visa card or a US bank account (about 125 EGP per bank withdrawal). PayPal's own Egypt page says linking an Egyptian Visa card or a US bank account enables receiving, but a 2024 report says Egyptians cannot receive international payments and the evidence conflicts. Wise receiving for Egypt residents is unverified. Expect 2-4 months from first paid run to cash (invoice on the 11th, payout on the 21st-25th of the following month, $20 minimum carry-over).

Narrower surviving form: drop 'breakage arbitrage' as the thesis. Survives only as (a) a free, zero-account demand-migration study, and (b) at most 1-3 clean-room Actors built on official or public JSON APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby job-board APIs; USAspending; SAM.gov; SEC EDGAR) in task classes where no working substitute with more than 20 users exists. These would be priced pay-per-event above compute, and the canary/regression loop would be kept as a Capability Genome reliability-receipt asset rather than a revenue claim. Expect pocket money at best; the strategic value is the reliability-receipts asset, not cash.

Poll the public Store API daily for 14 days for the 12 degraded high-demand Actors and their closest substitutes, and record 7-day and 30-day user counts and failure rates. If substitutes absorb more than 70% within 14 days, kill the breakage thesis. Phase 1 runs only if Phase 0 finds a lawful, logged-out, official-API task class with demand of at least 50 users and no working substitute of at least 20 users. In that case the founder completes Apify KYC, and one clean-room pay-per-event Actor is published, priced above measured compute, with a daily canary. Success is at least 1 non-self paying user within 30 days and a payout received through PayPal or SWIFT to Egypt within 60 days. The real gate being tested is whether the Egypt payout physically arrives.

verdicts.name: Novation Radar: small-business eligibility-transfer and early-recompete intelligence from FPDS/USAspending
strongestObjections: The 'early recompete' thesis (category A) is legally overstated. Under 13 CFR 125.12 (fully effective 2026-01-17) and FAR 52.219-28, a disqualifying recertification on a single-award set-aside does NOT terminate the contract or rewrite its terms. The agency only loses goaling credit for future options and orders. Whether a CO declines options and recompetes is a discretionary decision with no published base rate. Selling 'recompete pressure' as a forecast is therefore unsupported and risks being a false claim. The only hard, rule-based effect is on set-aside MACs: the firm is ineligible for future set-aside or reserved orders.

The signal source is mis-specified. Most GovCon M&A is structured as stock purchases or reverse triangular mergers specifically to avoid novation (PilieroMazza), so FPDS code J captures a minority of deals. The correct universe is J plus P (Rerepresentation of Non-Novated Merger/Acquisition) plus R (Rerepresentation). FPDS already ships a government-wide 'Rerepresentation Report' for exactly those three codes, and GovTribe exposes reason-for-modification as a searchable attribute. The raw event is not unpackaged; only the legal-consequence classification is new.

The Apify pay-per-event tier is a dead channel. Existing USAspending actors on the Apify Store show 1 monthly active user each (Fed Spend: 2 total users / 1 MAU; USASpending Scraper: 8 total / 1 MAU). Apify also deducts platform usage costs from pay-per-event payouts on top of its 20% commission. Expect roughly $0 from this tier.

Buyers are already served or do the work in-house. GovTribe sells federal data at $1,500-$6,000 per year, and GovWin and BGov sell at enterprise prices. M&A counsel such as PilieroMazza, Spencer Fane and Bean Kinney already perform novation and recertification diligence as billable legal work. A foreign, unknown, single-person vendor selling 'inferred' size status to compliance-sensitive buyers faces high trust friction. A $300 brief from an unknown source would not be relied on in a deal over counsel's own FPDS pull.

There is no live distribution. The 53 mailboxes started warming on 2026-10-21 and are weeks from send-ready, and GovCon BD and legal audiences are heavily prospected. With no inbound channel (SEO or community), the 45-day experiment would mostly measure silence.

Copyability is high. Any GovCon data vendor that already ingests mod-reason codes (GovTribe, HigherGov) could add a 'J/P/R + set-aside' alert in days if demand appeared. The 'moat' is only three legal rules encoded in a classifier.

Surviving narrow form: a free or cheap weekly 'Set-Aside Eligibility Shock' digest covering J/P/R modifications on set-aside MACs and single-award set-asides. It would state only the rule-certain consequences (loss of set-aside order eligibility on the MAC, loss of goaling credit, SBIR Phase III lineage status), with no recompete forecast. It would be sold as a data feed to small GovCon M&A advisors and boutique law firms via Payoneer or PayPal invoices, and used mainly as a lead magnet. Expected value is tiny; treat it as an option, not a revenue line.

FPDS ships a government-wide 'Rerepresentation Report' returning J, P and R modifications, with drill-down by agency and office. Its public accessibility is unclear and it may require an FPDS account (https://www.fpds.gov/help/about_reports/help_Rerepresentation_Report.html)

verdicts.name: Revenue-Defect Disclosure Market: Error Economy for non-security defects, paid by portfolio liability-bearers
strongestObjections: The flagship defect looks like a false positive. The receipt rates Reliant Plumbing's 'call button labelled 512-975-3085 dials 512-222-6029' as severity 5 with confidence 0.98. Public schema data, a directory listing and Cortera all list (512) 222-6029 as Reliant's own main line. So the button dials the business, not a stranger. Displaying one number while linking another (usually a call-tracking number) is common practice. In that case the loss is call attribution, not revenue, and a recipient running the '30-second disproof' would reach their own office and dismiss the sender. The candidate's own kill rule (more than 1 in 20 findings disproved) may already be hit by its best example.

The bounty framing closely matches the security world's 'beg bounty': unsolicited automated-scan findings followed by a hint of payment. Sophos and Commonwealth Bank tell small businesses not to engage with these. Free first disclosure plus an offer of a per-defect bounty will be filtered as that pattern, or as spam, whatever the guardrails say. The bounty language should be dropped entirely.

The franchisor payer is weak. Large home-service franchisors (Authority Brands with Marchex, Home Franchise Concepts with Invoca, CallTrackingMetrics and Avidtrak customers) already run enterprise call tracking that routes and records every call by location, including unanswered calls. Number control is centralized there, not on brittle tel links. Selling to a franchisor means a long enterprise cycle, and a stranger working from Egypt with no track record will not get through procurement inside 6 months.

The agency payer has cheap substitutes. Oh Dear charges $15 to $220 a month for 5 to 200 sites, SiteLetter about $5 per site, and Pingvera (free up to 5 sites) checks broken links and test-submits forms. A $99 to $399 a month 'portfolio watch' must beat these with defect classes those tools miss: tel-label mismatch, JSON-LD parse failure, dead form hosts. Of those, only dead forms and dead or disconnected numbers clearly lose revenue.

Revenue loss cannot be proven without an external effect. A misroute is only established by placing a call or submitting a form, which counts as contact or a test lead and needs authority. Static and headless witnesses prove that the label and the link disagree, not that a call was lost. The 62% first-answer booking figure comes from a vendor.

Narrower survivable form: drop the bounty and the 'Error Economy' market. Ship this as an evidence add-on to the existing Agency Revenue Leak Proof Pack and agency monitoring offer, sold only to agencies of record. Assert only classes with near-zero false positives: unparseable JSON-LD, form actions posting to dead hosts or 404s, and tel targets that do not match any number the business publicly lists anywhere. Downgrade a tel mismatch to ASK_DONT_ASSERT whenever either number appears in the business's own schema, GBP or directory data.

This candidate is correlated with the existing outreach wedge. It shares the payer (home-service agencies), the data source (the Inquiry Path Coherence engine), the delivery rail (the same 53 mailboxes, warming since 2026-10-21) and the main failure mode (cold-email reply rates). It is not an independent bet, and nothing can be sent until mid-November.

Payment rail is partly verified. Payoneer request-payment lets clients pay by card, ACH or bank transfer into a Payoneer balance, and an Egyptian user reports withdrawing to a local bank, but there is no current Egypt fee schedule. PayPal's official Egypt page says receiving requires an Egyptian Visa card or a US bank account, not a standard Egyptian bank account, so PayPal is a weak backup.

portfolioThesis: Under pessimistic assumptions, none of the six finalists has a positive p50 monthly contribution. Each has a mechanism probability of 0.07-0.15, and no payer is validated. Six names are really about three independent bets. (1) A US public-data obligation-inference bet: Single Audit Radar and Novation share ingestion, payer class, cold-email channel and Payoneer rail. (2) An inquiry-path defect bet: Claim Exchange and Disclosure Market share the IPC engine, buyer and mailboxes with the existing agency wedge, so they are one bet. (3) An Apify-marketplace rail bet, shared by the narrowed Claim Exchange actor, the Foundry and Novation. The EGP Holonomy switch is uncorrelated with these, but it produces no income; its value is calibration research for the Sovereign Forecast Engine. The right allocation is therefore not 'pick the winner'. It is three $0 experiments, each designed so that failing still leaves a durable asset. The first is a precision firewall that stops UberBond from making false 'lost calls' claims (second-witness falsification, #0653/#0306). The second is a hash-chained forecast ledger for federal obligations, scored against reality, which applies Prediction Accounting (#0059) and the Missing-Market Detector (#0178). The third is a marketplace observatory that decides whether, and which, single actor is worth publishing to prove the Egypt payout rail. The binding constraints are external and shared: an Egypt-receivable payout rail (Payoneer/Apify), and mailboxes that will not be send-ready until about mid-November. One payout proof and one bounded willingness-to-pay probe unblock most of the portfolio at once, so they outrank any additional building. Kill rules are pre-registered, and DNI mismatches and recompete forecasts are excluded from anything assertable.
